long_biography.plain_text:
Economics led Spiro J. Latsis into the financial side of an already substantial family enterprise. His father, John S. Latsis, had progressed from trading and shipbroking into shipping, refining, construction, property and banking. After doctoral study at the London School of Economics, Spiro joined the banking arm and later helped build EFG into an international private-banking group.

Spiro assumed direction of the wider interests after his father's death, chairing banking, energy and holding-company boards while the family remained invested across several sectors. A later succession moved representation of EFG's majority shareholder to his son John. Spiro continues as an EFG Bank Monaco director and president of the family foundation's supervisory board. His wealth reflects inheritance followed by substantial stewardship and expansion; bank assets under management, corporate property and foundation resources remain separate from his personal holdings.

Spiro Latsis is alive in current EFG and foundation governance. The stored 2003 death year belongs to his father, John S. Latsis. The dossier proposes correcting mortality to Alive; the unsupported death year should be cleared during review, but the schema does not support a blank-value proposal.

EFG and Forbes confirm 1946, but do not establish the exact day or birthplace. Wikipedia and Wikidata report 1 January and Athens. Athens remains review-only below threshold; the existing first-January date should not be treated as primary-source verified, and the existing Switzerland birth country is not independently supported.

Forbes reports that the siblings divided the family fortune in 2019, and EFG later transferred principal representation of its majority shareholder to Spiro's son John. Current public sources do not provide a complete asset-by-asset map of Spiro's personal ownership after those changes.

EFG shares are held through family-controlled intermediate companies, while Lamda properties, EFG client assets under management, energy-company assets and foundation resources belong to separate entities. They are not treated as solely or directly owned by Spiro Latsis.

Banking remains highly visible, but current evidence also connects the family platform to property, energy and other investments. Diversified is retained because no complete post-division personal allocation establishes one sector as dominant.
The existing exact-person Wikipedia link is valid and the dedicated Forbes profile is proposed. No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the acceptance threshold.
